The dominant signal is Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260), which achieved FDR 3.1e-16 with 7 matched inputs (fold enrichment 663×) in RaMP multi-DB ORA, ranked first by Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p=0.023, 8/8 matched compounds), and captured 4 of those same metabolites in the MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA overlay. Choline (C00114) and O-phospho-L-serine (C01005) are the primary drivers, flanked by sarcosine (C00213), S-adenosyl-L-methionine (C00019), (R)-lipoic acid (C16241), L-cystathionine (C02291), and AMP (C00020). The WikiPathways super-pathway 'Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways' (WP:WP2525) directly links these six compounds through the folate cycle, glycine cleavage, and cystathionine-shunt branches, and hit with FDR 8.8e-14. A secondary cluster — Methionine and Cysteine Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270) — is anchored by SAM (C00019), L-cystathionine (C02291), and O-phospho-L-serine (C01005), achieving raw p=0.0009 in MetaboAnalystR and consistent Mummichog enrichment at p=0.083. Glycerophospholipid Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00564) provides a third minor axis, with phosphorylcholine (C00588), choline (C00114), and cholesterol (C00187) producing p=0.02 (MetaboAnalystR) and p=0.041 (Mummichog). The biological story is one of coordinated disruption at the serine-glycine-one-carbon hub, which feeds both methylation (SAM) and trans-sulfuration (cystathionine) with downstream consequences for phospholipid remodeling and nucleotide supply.
